ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZS6T6A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC6D10", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 17, "title": "Implement S-DSP PMON pitch modulation and bounded pitch-counter advancement", "body": "## Problem

The S-DSP stores writes to PMON (`$2D`) but never uses them. Every voice advances solely from its own pitch registers, so software requesting modulation receives independent-pitch playback.

At baseline `5d4e89486b09ba130c6b8eb2a7159eccb4f1dc20`, [Dsp::sample](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5d4e89486b09ba130c6b8eb2a7159eccb4f1dc20/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L120-L241) processes voices in order, constructs an unmodulated 14-bit pitch at lines 217–218, and immediately consumes decoded samples through its fractional phase loop. The post-envelope output needed for modulation is calculated at line 231 but is not passed to the following voice.

This is a missing standard hardware function with existing prerequisites: BRR playback, interpolation, envelopes, shared noise and guest DSP-register access already exist. Correct high-pitch counter handling is included because modulation can produce increments above the base register's 14-bit range.

## Expected outcome

Implement sample-level PMON behavior throughout the existing generic DSP path.

### Hardware semantics

Use the PMON entry in [Fullsnes, SNES APU DSP Control Registers](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm) and the pitch-modulation/counter description in [Anomie's S-DSP Doc, jwdonal revision 1212, SOUND GENERATION](https://gist.github.com/nyanpasu64/a0d916ce6924912a7116682bf778e9a0). These specification links are already attributed by the repository's [DSP validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5d4e89486b09ba130c6b8eb2a7159eccb4f1dc20/docs/issue-15-validation.md#specification-attribution-and-independent-derivations). Record the relevant sections and independent numerical derivations in the implementation's validation evidence.

- PMON bits 1–7 enable modulation for their corresponding voices, using the immediately preceding voice. Bit 0 has no modulation effect; voice 0 does not wrap around to voice 7.
- Start with `p = PITCHL | ((PITCHH & 0x3F) << 8)`. For an enabled voice, use the preceding voice's signed, full-resolution output after source selection, envelope scaling and even-sample truncation, before left/right volume multiplication. Do not reconstruct that output from the eight-bit OUTX register, use mixed output, or reuse the preceding sample period's value.
- With arithmetic right shifts and sufficiently wide signed intermediates, calculate:

  ```text
  increment = p + (((previous_output >> 5) * p) >> 10)
  ```

  With modulation disabled, `increment = p`. Preserve the specified order of truncation. Do not mask or clamp the resulting increment back to `$3FFF`.
- Implement the documented bounded interpolation-position advancement, equivalent to `min((position & $3FFF) + increment, $7FFF)`, with the associated BRR decode progression. Adapt the current scalar phase representation as necessary; unrestricted repeated nibble consumption is not sufficient evidence for high modulated rates.
- Process modulation through successive adjacent voices within the logical output sample. An inactive, key-delayed or silenced-by-envelope predecessor supplies zero; early returns must not accidentally retain another voice's output. Release continues to contribute its actual output. Voice volumes and final FLG mute do not remove the modulation input.
- A noise-selected predecessor contributes its post-envelope noise output. A noise-selected target still advances its underlying BRR/pitch state using PMON, while its audible source remains the shared noise generator. Modulation must not alter that generator's rate or phase.
- Live PMON writes take effect at the existing sample API boundary without restarting voices, envelopes, BRR state or the shared rate/noise counters. Preserve pitch-register contents and existing register readback.

Useful independently calculated arithmetic anchors are:

| Base pitch | Predecessor output | Increment |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `$1000` | 0 | `$1000` |
| `$1000` | -32768 | `$0000` |
| `$1000` | -32512 | `$0020` |
| `$1000` | 32766 | `$1FFC` |
| `$1001` | -2 | `$0FFC` |
| `$3FFF` | 32766 | `$7FEE` |

The signed endpoints are arithmetic boundary vectors, not claims that every endpoint is reachable through every envelope configuration. Also test counter saturation explicitly: position `$3FFF` plus increment `$7FEE` produces `$7FFF`, without wrapping.

### Scope and remaining work

Include PMON routing, signed arithmetic, the minimum pitch-counter/BRR bookkeeping needed for its full increment range, numerical tests and original guest integration. Preserve PMON-disabled behavior and existing game regressions.

DSP subcycle register sampling, writes between voice-processing slots, torn pitch-register writes, SPC bus timing and register/RAM races remain outside this Issue. Exhaustive BRR filters/interpolation phases, hidden-envelope corrections and reference echo saturation also remain outstanding. Do not add a cycle-accurate DSP scheduler, unrelated frontend changes, firmware or per-game exceptions.

Every supplied inventory category retains its scope and outstanding work. Completing this Issue must not mark untested behavior verified or imply full DSP accuracy, commercial compatibility, or completion of historical partial Issue #3 work.

## Context and reproduction

The supplied open-Issue list is empty. This extends the missing PMON behavior rather than duplicating completed direct-color #11, envelope-rate #13 or noise #15 work.

Relevant inspected evidence:

- [DSP implementation and existing numerical tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5d4e89486b09ba130c6b8eb2a7159eccb4f1dc20/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs): register storage, ordered voice processing, signed envelope output, interpolation, key delay and BRR tests.
- [Noise interaction tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5d4e89486b09ba130c6b8eb2a7159eccb4f1dc20/crates/snes-core/src/dsp_noise_tests.rs#L233-L329): independent fixed pitches, continued BRR/ENDX processing during noise, release and reset continuity. They do not exercise PMON.
- [APU DSP access and cadence](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5d4e89486b09ba130c6b8eb2a7159eccb4f1dc20/crates/snes-core/src/apu.rs#L107-L205): one DSP sample every 32 SPC cycles and `$F2/$F3` register access.
- [Original noise guest and partition tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5d4e89486b09ba130c6b8eb2a7159eccb4f1dc20/crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_noise.rs): reusable patterns for bounded firmware-free upload, numerical register/PCM assertions and irregular master-clock partitioning.

Reproduce with two original BRR voices: keep voice 0 audible internally but set its stereo volumes to zero; give voice 1 a nonconstant waveform and nonzero base pitch. Compare PMON `$00` against `$02` using identical initial state. Assert independently derived voice-1 progression and PCM/OUTX checkpoints. The current implementation produces the same trajectory because it never reads PMON. Non-silence or a changed audio hash alone is insufficient.

This evaluation inspected repository files only and did not execute tests. Historical validation results are preservation context, not freshly verified results or PMON evidence.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the specified PMON routing, arithmetic and bounded counter/decode advancement. Keep the production change focused on DSP behavior and necessary phase bookkeeping.
- [ ] Add original numerical tests covering each enable bit 1–7, ignored bit 0, no voice-7-to-voice-0 wrap, unselected voices, adjacent modulation chains and a zero predecessor between nonzero voices. Include a changing predecessor that distinguishes current-sample output from stale output.
- [ ] Exercise the arithmetic anchors, zero pitch, masked PITCHH bits, both signed rounding directions, effective increments above `$3FFF`, and `$7FFF` position saturation. Assert actual phase/decode progression and selected PCM/OUTX/ENDX results using independently derived expectations. Expectations must not call production modulation/phase helpers or be recorded from emulator output.
- [ ] Verify full-resolution pre-volume modulation using predecessor samples that share OUTX but differ in relevant low bits. Changing predecessor stereo volumes or final mute must not change target progression. Cover zero envelope, inactive/key-delay states, release, retrigger and live PMON enable/disable without phase reset.
- [ ] Cover a noise predecessor and a noise-selected target, including underlying BRR looping/termination and ENDX. Preserve the existing shared-noise sequence, rate phase and PMON-disabled noise assertions.
- [ ] Add `crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_pitch.rs` with a bounded original SPC700 guest uploaded through the existing firmware-free protocol. It must write PMON through `$F2/$F3`, change PMON without KON, and produce independently calculated target OUTX/ENDX or PCM checkpoints that distinguish enabled and disabled modulation. Bound upload acknowledgements, checkpoint waits and total execution; require no core error and finite, normalized PCM.
- [ ] Add APU integration comparing every PCM sample and all DSP registers for whole versus irregularly partitioned master-clock advances, applying live changes at identical boundaries. Include independent numerical checkpoints; agreement between two emulator runs alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Record a baseline failure of the focused PMON reproduction against `5d4e89486b09ba130c6b8eb2a7159eccb4f1dc20` and its passing result after implementation. Update README limitations and validation evidence with exact commands, expected/actual results and remaining gaps. Document original guest/BRR code and data under MIT in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; any additional external fixture must have explicit source pins and licensing.
- [ ] Pass the following checks before merge, using the documented Rust/compiler selection and alternate browser port if needed:

  ```sh
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
  cargo test --workspace --locked
  cargo test -p snes-core --test dsp_pitch --locked
  python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
  cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
  python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
  python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
    --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
    --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
    --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
  python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
  python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
  python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
  npm --prefix web ci
  npm --prefix web run build
  (cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
  (cd web && npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds')
  ```

- [ ] Preserve existing fixture pins/hashes, assertions and replay durations. The browser gate must retain both cleared 18,100-frame game replays, Castle's complete map/credits route, Memory's numerical and live-audio checks, and existing diagnostic/browser checks. The grep exclusion applies only to optional unaudited games. No commercial ROM or firmware acquisition is required.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
